coins.name: Catecoin

coins.who: A tiny rescued kitten that Atsuko Sato, owner of Kabosu (the Shiba Inu behind Doge), shared in a short video on 26 Jul 2026. MarsBit/CoinW call the kitten Momo; a July 2026 Osso Magazine interview names Sato's newest rescue Rika-chan, so the name is unconfirmed. Sato says her post was used without permission and she has no ties to CATE. The logo is an illustrated tabby kitten.
coins.lore: In July 2026 Atsuko Sato, whose photos of Kabosu became Doge, shared a short clip of a tiny rescued kitten. Within hours, strangers on Solana launched CATE, 'the cat sister of Dogecoin': Dog plus E, Cat plus E. Its first dev drifted away and the community carried it on. Sato has said she has no connection to CATE and did not agree to her post being used. So here the kitten stays what it really is: a small rescue with eyes closed and chin up, and a reminder that the best cat stories start with someone taking a cat home.

coins.name: Popcat
coins.catName: Oatmeal (Pop Cat)
coins.who: Oatmeal, a real domestic short-haired cat owned by Twitter user @XavierBFB. In October 2020 two photos of him, one calm and one edited into a huge 'O' mouth, were shared on Discord. A friend's edit reached r/MEOW_IRL on Oct 9 and Twitter on Oct 10, 2020, becoming the 'Pop Cat' meme and, in December 2020, the popcat.click game.
coins.lore: Oatmeal never set out to be famous. In October 2020 a friend of his human turned two snapshots of him, one calm and one with a comically round 'O' mouth, into a looping gif, and the internet began singing through him. Within weeks he was lip-syncing to every song imaginable. That December three University of Sheffield students built popcat.click, and whole countries raced to pop him the most, with Taiwan, Thailand and Hong Kong trading the top spot. Hundreds of billions of pops later, the little white cat with the tabby cap is still the internet's favourite click.

loreSource.label: The sanctuary's research on this cat

viral.summary: The two-frame 'pop' loop spread from Reddit to Twitter in October 2020, then became lip-sync edits on Instagram and iFunny ('wide-mouth singing cat'). popcat.click, built on Dec 11, 2020 by three University of Sheffield students, turned it into a country-vs-country clicking race: Brazil (Feb 2021), Finland (Apr 2021, where schools banned it), then Taiwan, Thailand and Malaysia (Aug 2021). Google's 2021 Year in Search listed Popcat as the top trending game.

coins.disclaimer: Unofficial fan card. Catcoin Sanctuary is not affiliated with Popcat, popcat.click, Oatmeal or his owner. Not financial advice: memecoins are highly volatile and can go to zero. Always check the contract address yourself.

coins.name: Hello Kitty
coins.catName: Hello Kitty (Kitty White), Sanrio's character
coins.who: Hello Kitty, real name Kitty White, is the character Yuko Shimizu created for Japan's Sanrio in 1974; she first appeared on a vinyl coin purse in March 1975. Sanrio's story makes her a kind girl from a London suburb, drawn in the motif of a white cat with a red bow and no visible mouth. This coin is an unofficial fan memecoin, not affiliated with Sanrio.
coins.lore: Hello Kitty has been saying hello since 1975, when Sanrio put a little white cat with a red bow on a vinyl coin purse in Japan, sitting between a bottle of milk and a goldfish bowl. Her story says she is Kitty White, a kind girl from a London suburb who loves baking cookies and her twin sister Mimmy. Fifty years on, a group of fans on Solana made a coin in her honour, called themselves Hello Kitty Fans and chose a simple pink bow as their badge. It is an unofficial tribute: Sanrio has nothing to do with it, and the fans say so up front.

loreSource.label: The sanctuary's research on this cat

viral.summary: Hello Kitty is one of the most successful characters ever made. Wikipedia cites about $5 billion a year by 2010 and roughly $8 billion at retail in 2013, over 50,000 branded products by 2008, a UNICEF children's ambassador role, and her 2008 appointment as Japan's tourism ambassador to China and Hong Kong, the first time the ministry picked a fictional character. The coin is a small fan tribute to that fame: fan accounts @HKittyOnSol (May 2025) and @hkittycoin (November 2025) run it, and after early IP worries it switched to a plain pink bow as its logo (Bitget Wallet).

coins.lore: Maneki is the beckoning cat of Japanese shop counters: a white lucky cat with one paw raised to wave good fortune in through the door. The best-known legend sets it at Gotoku-ji temple in Edo-era Tokyo, where a cat beckoned a passing lord inside moments before a storm broke. The Solana MANEKI keeps the classic look, red ears, a red collar and a gold bell, and adds a blissful closed-eye smile. Since April 2024 it has waved from Solana and, for the 2024/25 season, from the red-and-white shirts of Sheffield United.

coins.name: GTA6CAT (Gato)
coins.catName: Gato, the bodega cat on the ATM in Grand Theft Auto VI Trailer 2
coins.who: A fictional, computer-animated brown tabby in Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI Trailer 2 (6 May 2025): it sits on top of a bodega's ATM, grooming itself as Jason buys beer (spotted by PC Gamer). It has no name in the game; 'Gato' (Spanish for cat) and its backstory come from the coin's fans. Not a real pet; the character is Rockstar's IP.
coins.lore: Gato is the bodega cat of Vice City. In the second Grand Theft Auto VI trailer he sits on top of a corner-store ATM and calmly washes himself while Jason buys beer, a few quiet seconds in a trailer full of chaos. Fans noticed, and the cat on the ATM became a small legend. His fan site tells the rest: nobody knows where he came from, the clerk thinks he runs the store, and Gato has never once moved for anyone. One cat, nine lives, zero concerns, and the best seat in the shop.

loreSource.label: The sanctuary's research on this cat

viral.summary: The cat is a few seconds of background in a record trailer launch: Rockstar said GTA VI Trailer 2 drew 475 million views across platforms in its first 24 hours. PC Gamer's round-up of the trailer's animals (8 May 2025) singled out the bodega cat on the ATM. In August 2026, amid GTA VI gameplay leaks and two days before Rockstar's first official gameplay reveal (27 Aug), fans launched $GATO on pump.fun (25 Aug). X's trending card 'GTA VI Cats Turn Skeptics into Eager Fans' (28 Aug) recapped the cat posts of those days, noting trailers that show cats grooming on ATMs. The coin's site parodies Rockstar's as 'Grand Theft Gato VI', the story of a cat who owns the store.

coins.lore: Stonk Cats are 1,111 cats who never left the trading floor. Each one has its own face, fur and outfit: sharp suits, miner helmets, hoodies, paper-bag disguises, each posed by a rainy bodega window, a diner booth or a bank vault after hours. The face of the coin is cat #0055, a blue-grey tabby in hot-pink shield sunglasses and a navy track jacket, cheekily sticking out its tongue in a late-night diner. coins.name: Hosico
coins.catName: Hosico, the golden Scottish Straight of Moscow (@hosico_cat)
coins.who: Hosico is a real male golden Scottish Straight ('black golden ticked'), born 4 August 2014 in Russia, who lives in Moscow with Roman and Ksenia. Their daughter, a fan of Japan, named him 'star child'. They began posting him on Instagram as a kitten; he had 662,000 followers by 2017 and about 1.7-1.9 million later, loved for his hamster cheeks and huge round eyes.
coins.lore: Hosico is a golden Scottish Straight from Moscow with round hamster cheeks and huge, dreamy eyes. His family brought him home as a shy little kitten after losing their old Siamese, Misha, and their daughter, who loved Japan, named him Hosico: star child. He hides when the doorbell rings, tires of new toys within a week, adores a drinking straw and a bit of black rope, and chatters at his people when playtime ends. Fans compare him to Puss in Boots and Garfield; the coin's artists imagine him as a glowing star child who gathers forgotten dreams.

loreSource.label: The sanctuary's research on this cat

viral.summary: Hosico is one of Instagram's best-known cats, a round-faced golden fluff that fans compare to Puss in Boots, Garfield or a giant hamster. The Purrington Post counted 662,000 Instagram followers at his third birthday (2017), Munchiecat 1.9 million in 2022, and he was nominated for The Animal Star of 2020. The coin borrowed his name on letsbonk.fun in April 2025 and became one of that launchpad's biggest tokens by July 2025. In January 2026 the project moved to a new contract and retold him as 'Star Child', a glowing orange kitten with a star on his chest who gathers forgotten dreams.

coins.who: An unnamed brown tabby kitten from a photo, mouth open mid-'roar', with a red headband added: the headband is Keith Gill's trademark from his Roaring Kitty GameStop livestreams. On 11 May 2026 this picture became the profile photo of Gill's X account @TheRoaringKitty (1.6M followers), and it still is. The kitten's owner and the photo's origin are unknown.
coins.lore: Red Kitten Crew is a tiny brown tabby kitten, mouth wide open in its fiercest roar, with a red headband tied across its forehead. The headband is a nod to Keith Gill, the GameStop trader known as Roaring Kitty, whose red headband became a symbol of the 2021 retail rally. On 11 May 2026 this kitten appeared as his X profile picture, where it still sits today. The posts that came with it vanished within the hour and he has never explained them, but a crew of fans kept the kitten, tied on their own red headbands and made it their mascot.

loreSource.label: The sanctuary's research on this cat

viral.summary: At about 21:13 UTC on 11 May 2026, after 16 months of silence, Keith Gill's verified @TheRoaringKitty account switched its picture to this kitten and posted RKC's pump.fun address with a short cat clip; a follow-up read 'red bandit crew 4 life'. The posts were deleted within roughly 30-60 minutes. RKC jumped to about $11-12M in market value within minutes and then crashed; Lookonchain said the developer's wallets exited with about $729k, and many traders suspected a hacked account. Gill has made no statement. The kitten is still his avatar, and holders now run RKC as a community takeover ('tie the band').
